A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PRESELECT and contain readable corresponding text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Renamed baselines and material shifted by pagination can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model pretraining evaluations on RefinedWeb and C4, alongside analyses of selected documents and learned fastText features.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds evaluations and diagnostic analyses of the PPL Correlation (DP) comparator.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same predictive-strength equation, six Llama scoring models, positive/negative document selection, and fastText filtering pipeline. v3 explains the existing model choice; its added DP procedure is a comparator, not a modification to PRESELECT.

E1.justification: RefinedWeb, C4, and the downstream task coverage remain unchanged, including Math and Code BPC evaluations. The new comparator uses existing coverage; discussion of raw versus processed corpora concerns positioning against cited work.

E2.justification: v1's PPL Correlation is retained as PPL Correlation (DD). v3 adds PPL Correlation (DP), which trains fastText from domain-level labels for page-level selection, to the 1B/30B-token comparison and the feature/domain analyses in Tables 3–4. Other comparator memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 2.3 newly reports preliminary trials using scoring models from multiple families, adding a model-configuration test, although the models and prompts are unspecified. Existing benchmark budgets, selection ratios, architectures, metrics, and appendix protocols remain unchanged; DP uses the retained 1B/30B-token setting.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 extend the learned-feature and selected-domain analyses to DP, examining what its classifier learns and selects. Section 2.3 also adds a qualitative account of unsuccessful mixed-family scoring trials. Existing seed-data, feature, domain, and document-length analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, random-seed reporting, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. v3's discussion of evaluation noise does not introduce quantified uncertainty or a statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds DP results: Table 1 reports a 29.3 average versus 28.1 for Random and 33.4 for PRESELECT under the same setting. It also adds DP feature/domain values and the qualitative mixed-family failure finding. Existing numerical results remain unchanged. Prose correctly replaces ARC-Easy decline examples with HellaSwag/ARC-Challenge: Table 11 shows 36.3 versus 40.0 and 23.7 versus 24.4, respectively.

T1.justification: The compression formulation, predictive-strength definition in Equation 1, and fastText feature-contribution derivation in Appendix A.3 are unchanged. New acknowledgment of prior ranking-based correlation work adds no mathematical definition, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction qualifies novelty by explicitly placing PRESELECT within Perplexity Correlation's framework and acknowledging concurrent document-level experiments. It adds the six-model choice as a distinguishing contribution. The central predictive-data hypothesis, performance, scalability, and compute-saving claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 newly attributes mixed-family scoring failures to prompt-dependent evaluation noise and conjectures that this explains differences from cited results. Sections 3.4 and 4.2–4.3 explain DP's remaining weaknesses through noisy domain-level labels, while acknowledging that page-level selection mitigates DD's limitations. These are additional interpretations, not established causal demonstrations.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C retain the scoring-model list, fastText hyperparameters and end-token adjustment, hardware, training configurations, evaluation frameworks, and code/data access information. The new comparator receives a broad procedural description, without additional concrete implementation settings or reproducibility instructions.

R1.justification: The relationship to the closest prior work is substantially revised. v1 describes shared intuition and emphasizes document-level selection versus domain selection. v3 explicitly credits Perplexity Correlation's foundational framework and earlier ranking-based metrics, acknowledges its concurrent document-level and 1B experiments, and develops distinctions involving model-family choice and processed data pools. The bibliography itself is essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted rewrites and explanatory expansions in the introduction, method rationale, and comparator discussion. It also corrects the author-name order, the abstract's stray 'emph' text, and Appendix A.3.2's broken table reference. The section hierarchy and most prose remain stable.

P2.justification: Tables 1, 3, and 4 expand with DP rows, and Figure 2 is restyled while depicting the same pipeline. Other figures and appendix displays are retained with pagination shifts. Table 3 introduces a labeling error: the DP row containing negative influence scores is also marked 'pos'.

improvement.justification: The added DP comparison and diagnostics make the closest-method comparison more informative, while explicit prior-work acknowledgment and corrected benchmark examples improve precision. These benefits strengthen the presentation of unchanged core results. Gains are limited by qualitative mixed-family evidence, missing full DP results in Appendix C, and the new Table 3 labeling error.
